name: Hidden Markov / Markov regime-switching models
summary: Assumes the data switch between a few hidden regimes (e.g. expansion and recession) and estimates when.
inputs: A univariate or multivariate series; number of regimes.
outputs: Regime-specific parameters, transition probabilities, filtered and smoothed regime probabilities.

data_requirements.min_observations: Long enough to contain several regime switches
data_requirements.missing_values: Not supported in most implementations; fill or trim

assumptions: A small number of discrete hidden regimes
Within-regime model (e.g. Gaussian mean/variance) is adequate
math_summary: Observations depend on an unobserved discrete state s_t following a Markov chain with transition matrix P; parameters estimated by maximum likelihood via the Hamilton filter or EM (Baum-Welch), giving filtered and smoothed regime probabilities.
when_to_use: Series with apparent switches in mean or volatility
when_not_to_use: Many regimes with little data (identification problems)
When regimes are known and observable
pitfalls: Label switching and local optima: use several starts
hmmlearn has had limited maintenance (last push Oct 2024)

compute.complexity: O(n K^2) per filter pass for K regimes.

applicability.use_case: Recession probabilities from GDP or employment growth (Hamilton's original application is US GNP)

materials.why: Brought Markov switching to economics using US GNP.
